historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah, vol. 9, p. 176. Ziyaam ibn Salamah was the chief judge of Egypt during the reign of the Abbasid Caliph Al-Mansur (754-775 CE). He was known for his religious knowledge, piety, and justice, and was highly respected by the Caliph and the people of Egypt.

Ibn Abd al-Hadid, Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah, vol. 6, p. 380. Ziyaam ibn Salamah was also a companion of Imam Ali Zain al-Abidin (604-661 CE), the fourth Shia Imam. He was known for his deep understanding of the Prophet Muhammad's traditions and sayings, and was a trusted advisor to Imam Zain al-Abidin.
